verses.pali: “Dasabalasamannāgato, bhikkhave, tathāgato catūhi ca vesārajjehi samannāgato āsabhaṁ ṭhānaṁ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṁ nadati, brahmacakkaṁ pavatteti—
verses.english: “Mendicants, a Realized One has ten powers and four kinds of self-assurance. With these he claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and turns the divine wheel.

verses.pali: iti rūpaṁ iti rūpassa samudayo iti rūpassa atthaṅgamo,
verses.english: Such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the ending of form.

verses.pali: iti vedanā iti vedanāya samudayo iti vedanāya atthaṅgamo,
verses.english: Such is feeling, such is the origin of feeling, such is the disappearance of feeling.

verses.pali: iti saññā iti saññāya samudayo iti saññāya atthaṅgamo,
verses.english: Such is perception, such is the origin of perception, such is the disappearance of perception.

verses.pali: iti saṅkhārā iti saṅkhārānaṁ samudayo iti saṅkhārānaṁ atthaṅgamo,
verses.english: Such are choices, such is the origin of choices, such is the disappearance of choices.

verses.pali: iti viññāṇaṁ iti viññāṇassa samudayo iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo.
verses.english: Such is consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the disappearance of consciousness.

verses.pali: Iti imasmiṁ sati idaṁ hoti, imassuppādā idaṁ uppajjati.
verses.english: When this exists, this comes to be; due to the arising of this, this arises.

verses.pali: Imasmiṁ asati idaṁ na hoti, imassa nirodhā idaṁ nirujjhati.
verses.english: When this doesn’t exist, this doesn’t come to be; due to the cessation of this, this ceases. That is:
Ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
When ignorance fades away and ceases with nothing left over, choices cease.
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”
